segments.narration: Nine hikers cut their tent open from inside. February 1959, the northern Urals. They ran out into minus thirty wearing almost nothing.
Searchers found them scattered down the slope. Two lay by a dead fire under a cedar, their hands burned from climbing it.
The injuries made it worse. Crushed ribs. A fractured skull. And almost no marks on the skin above them.
The file was sealed for decades, so the theories grew instead: secret weapons tests, infrasound, even a yeti.
In 2020 Russian prosecutors reopened it and named a slab avalanche. A year later physicists modelled the slope doing exactly that.
